# EDGAR Terminal

EDGAR Terminal is a free, source-linked research application for SEC filings, company fundamentals, reported fund holdings and official CFTC Commitments of Traders positioning. It is an educational research tool, not investment advice.

## Main research surfaces

- [Financial Analysis](https://secedgarterminal.com/analysis): full SEC company search and a small sector sampler, with server-rendered financial highlights at `/analysis/{ticker}`. Six business-specific metrics include current and comparable prior values, reporting periods, explicit units, calculated-versus-reported labels and original SEC sources. The interactive workspace provides full statements, evidence and scenarios.
- [Company scenario methodology](https://secedgarterminal.com/analysis/scenarios): server-rendered definitions, equations, units and evidence limits for operating scenarios, the optional connected cash model, historical context, sensitivity drivers and baseline updates. This guide contains methodology, not company forecasts or user scenario results. Company scenario URLs with `view=scenarios` remain noindex interactive selections; cite the canonical company financial brief for reported evidence and the guide for model definitions.

- [Market](https://secedgarterminal.com/market): macro market briefing combining filing-based sector fundamentals with separately sourced CFTC positioning. The three views are Market Briefing, CFTC Positioning and Sector Performance. Coverage counts companies, primary sectors and reported SEC SIC industries, with source dates and missing coverage kept explicit. Sector performance describes accounting fundamentals, not stock-market returns or national GDP.
- [CFTC Positioning](https://secedgarterminal.com/market?tab=positioning): separate futures-market context from official futures-only COT reports.
- [Sector Performance](https://secedgarterminal.com/market?tab=sectors): compare sector growth, margins, cash generation and capital intensity, with equal issuer weights and metric-specific observation counts.
- [Portfolio](https://secedgarterminal.com/workspace): upload a custom portfolio or explore the demo through Summary, Holdings, Financials, Concentration & Exposure, and What Changed. Shared markets compares SEC filing connections with separately sourced CFTC positioning; linked-company allocation is not measured market exposure.
- [Demo: What changed](https://secedgarterminal.com/workspace/demo/changes): server-rendered, dated SEC-linked CFTC market changes for the same 100-company demo universe used throughout the portfolio demo. Includes company checks, incomplete/stale coverage and original-source links; candidate market connections are not measured issuer exposures. Prepared results may not yet be available.
- [Funds & institutional managers](https://secedgarterminal.com/fund): links to server-rendered, source-dated fund and manager research briefs. Fund reports use `/fund/{ticker}` (optional `?accession=`); manager reports use `/fund/manager/{CIK}` (optional `?period=YYYY-MM-DD`). Briefs show prepared holdings, reporting coverage and freshness without requiring JavaScript. The interactive workspaces provide full holdings, comparisons and research tools.
- Prepared fund and manager briefs include Dataset structured metadata and an `application/json` alternate link to the same bounded summary. Prefer the canonical brief URL when citing research; cite its original SEC filing for filing facts. Preserve the reporting period and stale status. The directory lists available research routes, not a guarantee that every route has prepared coverage.
- [Filings](https://secedgarterminal.com/filings), [Analysis](https://secedgarterminal.com/analysis), [Risk](https://secedgarterminal.com/risk), [Compare](https://secedgarterminal.com/compare), [Funds](https://secedgarterminal.com/fund), and [Disclosures](https://secedgarterminal.com/disclosures).

## Active public data APIs

- `GET /api/v1/analysis/{ticker}?basis=annual|quarter|ytd|ttm&end=YYYY-MM-DD` — concise financial research from existing prepared data; defaults to annual and latest period. Cache-only: never starts SEC acquisition or stores another financial history. Preserves nulls, metric definitions, source concepts and filing dates. An older `end` uses the latest filed values for that period, not the information known at that date. A filing `asOf` cutoff is not prepared by this public endpoint and returns HTTP 503 without substituting current data; use the interactive workspace for historical vintage research. Unknown, duplicate or empty query fields return HTTP 400.

- `GET /api/v2/factor-universe?basis=ttm|annual` — prepared SEC-only fundamental universe used by shared research data services. Schema: `/schemas/factor-universe-v2.schema.json`.
- `GET /api/v1/cftc/markets?family=tff|disaggregated&date=latest|YYYY-MM-DD` — validated family catalog plus the curated launch-market snapshot. Schema: `/schemas/cftc-markets-v1.schema.json`.
- `GET /api/v1/cftc/history?family=...&contract=...&group=...&date=...&window=1y|3y|5y` — bounded single-contract history. Schema: `/schemas/cftc-history-v1.schema.json`.
- `GET /api/v1/cftc/market-comparison` — parameter-free, cache-only comparison of 25 curated public futures markets. Contains no portfolio holdings or allocations and never starts SEC/CFTC acquisition. TFF uses Leveraged Funds; Disaggregated uses Managed Money. Includes net/open interest, exact seven-day change in percentage points, and an observed trailing 52-week range. `range.position` is linear min/max placement, NOT a percentile. Preserve each report date, actual observation count and date span, nulls, and stale/incomplete flags. HTTP 200 may contain partial or entirely unavailable prepared coverage; preparation of every market is not guaranteed. All query parameters are rejected. Schema: `/schemas/portfolio-market-comparison-v1.schema.json`.
- `GET /api/v1/cftc/status` — cache-only family-level readiness for prepared CFTC snapshots. It recomputes cache age and report currency without contacting the upstream CFTC service.
- `GET /api/v1/cftc/portfolio-changes/demo?days=30` — read-only prepared public demo changes; accepts 1–90 days. It never starts SEC/CFTC acquisition. Preserve companyChecks, marketChecks, preparation status, coverage, observation dates and source evidence. HTTP 503 means prepared research is unavailable or disabled, not that no changes occurred.
- `GET /api/v1/funds/{ticker}?accession=...` — read-only prepared N-PORT summary, bounded to ten largest positions plus SEC sources. An optional exact accession selects a historical filing; it never silently substitutes the latest report. Does not start SEC acquisition. HTTP 503 means prepared coverage is unavailable.
- `GET /api/v1/managers/{CIK}?period=YYYY-MM-DD` — read-only prepared 13F manager summary, bounded to ten largest positions plus SEC sources. The optional period must be a completed calendar quarter. Does not start SEC acquisition. HTTP 503 means prepared coverage is unavailable.
- `GET /api/fund-13f/market-review?cik={CIK}&view=snapshot&period=YYYY-MM-DD` — read-only published manager market review; omit `period` for the latest saved quarter, which may differ from the latest available SEC report. The same publication appears on manager research pages without JavaScript. Preserve its publication version, portfolio quarter, full-portfolio denominator, coverage, source-check dates and incomplete or stale status. The first 50 holding summaries and up to three displayed issuer source examples are not the full reviewed universe. Supported connections describe issuer filing evidence and futures research benchmarks, not measured economic exposure or the manager’s own futures holdings. This GET never starts a source review.
- [OpenAPI document](https://secedgarterminal.com/openapi.json).

All active data endpoints are read-only. The factor-universe and CFTC markets/history endpoints are rate limited; the CFTC status endpoint is cache-only and never contacts the upstream service. Preserve response nulls, coverage counts, report dates, retrieval times, schema/calculation versions, stale or partial status, source URLs and formulas.

## Prepared SEC fundamental universe

- Schema version: `edgar.factor-universe.v2`.
- Methodology version: `fundamental-universe-2.0.0`.
- Supported measures are revenue-growth acceleration, operating margin, free-cash-flow margin, book equity/assets, net margin and cash/assets.
- Each unique CIK counts once and receives equal weight. Expanded coverage is based on published IVV, IJH and IJR equity holdings mapped to SEC issuers. It is a dated coverage proxy, not certified index membership or the whole market.
- Each metric requires current and compatible prior-year filing observations for the same issuer. Missing inputs remain null and stay outside that metric's denominator.
- Ratio changes use percentage points. Direction thresholds are sensitivity bands, not significance tests; neutral observations remain in the paired denominator.
- Breadth, median change, paired IQR change, cash confirmation and within/between-sector population variance are descriptive accounting statistics.
- Financial issuers are excluded from operating-margin, free-cash-flow-margin and cash/assets diagnostics where the measure is not comparable.
- No security-price, return, beta, volatility, correlation or post-filing market-response data enters v2.

## CFTC Positioning

- Schema version: `edgar.cftc-positioning.v1`.
- Calculation version: `cftc-positioning-1.0.0`.
- The only active upstream market-data source is the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission Public Reporting API.
- TFF uses official futures-only dataset `gpe5-46if`; Disaggregated uses official futures-only dataset `72hh-3qpy`.
- Report families and participant taxonomies stay separate. Canonical observations use family, report basis, exact contract code and report date; history comparisons additionally require a matching venue and unit regime. Standard, micro, consolidated, discontinued and replacement contracts are not silently combined.
- Net contracts = reported long contracts − reported short contracts. Net percentage of open interest = 100 × net contracts / open interest.
- Weekly and four-week changes require observations exactly 7 and 28 calendar days earlier. Prior-available comparisons are labeled separately; values are never forward-filled.
- Percentiles compare the selected observation only with compatible prior observations for that same contract and group. Ties receive half weight; later reports are excluded.
- Market-comparison ranges use valid observations within 52 × 7 calendar days through the selected report, including current. `range.position = 100 × (netPctOi − min) / (max − min)` is not a percentile or a cross-market ranking. A flat range or missing current value has no range position; fewer than two valid observations produce no range. Available observations may cover less than a full year. `generatedAt` is the comparison assembly time, not the source report date or source retrieval time.
- COT values are aggregated outstanding futures positions reported for a Tuesday, generally released later in the week. They are not individual trader records, traded volume, dollar flows, issuer exposure, equity prices or automatic buy/sell signals.
- Official guidance: https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/index.htm
- Official COT Help: https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/stories/s/COT-Help/p2fg-u73y/
- Official release schedule: https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/ReleaseSchedule/index.htm
- Official TFF resource: https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/resource/gpe5-46if.json
- Official Disaggregated resource: https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/resource/72hh-3qpy.json

## Retired contracts

- `GET /api/prices` returns HTTP 410.
- `GET /api/v1/market-signals` returns HTTP 410.
- `GET /api/v1/factor-universe` returns HTTP 410 and points to `/api/v2/factor-universe`.

These endpoints depended on retired third-party security-price acquisition and derived return analytics. CFTC positioning is not a replacement price feed, and retired v1 fields are not reinterpreted in v2.

## Interpretation and provenance

- Analysis highlights use six metrics selected for the corporate, banking or insurance business lens. Ratios and derived quarters/TTM are calculations, not directly reported facts. Percent values are already in percentage units; percentage changes and percentage-point differences are distinct. A missing value is not zero. The source check time is separate from the calculation time and financial reporting period.
- Analysis scenarios are same-period hypothetical counterfactuals, not forecasts, reported results, probabilities or investment recommendations. The connected corporate model adjusts reported operating cash flow and ending cash by modeled deltas; it never adds the entire reported operating cash flow to ending cash. Extra tax applies only to positive incremental earnings after incremental interest; negative changes receive no assumed tax relief. Explicit working-capital cash use, capex changes, borrowing and repayment remain user assumptions. New-borrowing interest uses the inclusive selected-period day count divided by 365. Negative hypothetical cash is an unfunded shortfall, not automatically filled borrowing; dependent funded balance-sheet outcomes are withheld. Missing inputs and incompatible accounting scopes stay explicit.
- Scenario driver rankings describe one-at-a-time bounded assumption shocks and depend on the chosen ranges and outcome. Historical ranges describe only supported comparable prior observations, not a probability distribution. CFTC observations remain separate market context and never automatically set earnings or price shocks. Public Analysis JSON endpoints return prepared financial evidence, not personal scenario settings or modeled outputs.

- N-PORT net assets and 13F reportable holdings value are different measures. A manager’s 13F value is not total assets under management, an individual fund’s net asset value, a complete portfolio or investment performance. Preserve option labels, security identifiers, missing values, reporting dates, amendments, confidential omissions and coverage limitations.
- A reporting period, filing date, CFTC report date, source retrieval time and application calculation time are different clocks.
- Aggregates describe the covered sample and expose their own eligible counts. A missing result is not evidence that an event, exposure or filing does not exist.
- Verify consequential figures and passages against the linked SEC or CFTC source.
- SEC filing facts, SEC filing text, N-PORT holdings and CFTC COT reports answer different questions and should not be blended without an explicit, documented research design.
